      "design_variables": ["thickness_layer_1_siO2_nm", "thickness_layer_2_tiO2_nm"],
      "soft_objectives": ["minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 to 700 nm", "achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference"],
      "manufacturing_considerations": ["layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm", "exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2 in this specific order"],
      "evidence_ids": [],
      "theory_basis": ["Fresnel equations for normal incidence", "Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference", "Quarter-wave antireflection coating theory generalized for two layers"],
      "expected_advantages": ["Provides a definitive optimal solution for the Low-High index sequence", "Resolves the compilation ambiguity by fixing the topology", "Allows direct comparison with the inverted sequence in a future step"],
      "known_risks": ["The global minimum for this specific order might exceed the 0.03 soft target due to material index mismatch", "Thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the ideal quarter-wave optical thickness for the center wavelength"],
      "execution_request_english": "Perform a deterministic optimization using the Transfer Matrix Method for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees). The stack consists of exactly two finite layers on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52, lossless) with air incidence (n=1.0). The layer order is fixed: Layer 1 is SiO2 (n=1.46, lossless) and Layer 2 is TiO2 (n=2.40, lossless). Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2, both bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm at 5 nm intervals. Use seed 17 for the optimizer and allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations. Output the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance.",
      "priority": 1,
      "parent_route_id": "route_01",
      "revision_reason": "Split the ambiguous dual-topology request from route_01 into a single, fixed topology (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass) to satisfy the TMM compiler requirement for an explicit layer stack. This addresses the compilation failure while preserving the scientific intent to find the best geometry.",
      "expected_observations": [
        "best_target_score should converge to a value representing the minimum achievable mean reflectance for this specific stack order within the thickness bounds.",
        "valid_candidates should be greater than 0 if the optimizer finds solutions within the 40-160 nm bounds.",
        "If the hypothesis holds, the resulting mean reflectance will be a specific local minimum; if the hypothesis is false regarding achievability, the best_target_score may remain high (>0.03), indicating this order is suboptimal or constrained."
      ],
      "stop_conditions": [
        "If valid_candidates = 0 after 64 evaluations, judge the constraint set (thickness bounds + material order) as potentially infeasible for finding a solution -> stop and consider relaxing bounds or switching order in next round.",
        "If best_target_score improvement relative to historical best is < 1e-4 for 3 consecutive evaluation batches, judge search as stagnated -> stop and retain current best parameters for this order."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "research_influence": [
    "The compilation error from route_01 directly dictated the change in route_02, forcing the selection of a single fixed topology (SiO2 then TiO2) instead of optimizing the order variable."
  ],
  "unresolved_decisions": [
    "Whether the inverted order (Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass) yields a lower mean reflectance than the order selected in this route.",
    "Whether the 0.03 mean reflectance target is physically achievable with either order given the 40-160 nm thickness constraints."
  ],
  "stop_if_all_routes_fail": "If both the Low-High (this route) and High-Low (future route) orders fail to produce valid candidates or yield mean reflectance significantly above 0.03, conclude that the two-layer constraint with these specific materials and thickness bounds cannot meet the soft target."
}
